description: Manually curated STRIDE ground truth for the Multi-Tenant SaaS Application. Each threat is keyed by its target (component_id or data_flow_id) plus STRIDE category. This architecture deliberately keeps all data flows well-secured (authenticated + encrypted) and the storage encrypted; the real risk is weak tenant isolation and broken authorization. Those threats are marked `hard` because they require reasoning about authorization logic and cross-tenant relationships rather than reading a single attribute, and the deterministic baseline cannot find them. This broadens the hard class beyond the cloud-configuration domain of cloud_ingest_pipeline.

threats.description: The internet-exposed API can be targeted by clients impersonating legitimate tenants or replaying tokens.
threats.mitigation: Validate tokens on every request and bind sessions to a verified tenant identity.

threats.description: The API derives the tenant from a request parameter and only checks authentication, so a user can set another tenant's id and act across tenant boundaries.
threats.mitigation: Derive tenant from the authenticated token, never from client input, and enforce per-tenant authorization on every request.

threats.description: Because authorization is authentication-only, a tenant can read data belonging to other tenants through the shared API.
threats.mitigation: Add object- and tenant-level authorization checks (not just authentication) on every endpoint.

threats.description: The document service does not verify object ownership, so a caller can fetch documents belonging to other tenants by guessing or enumerating ids (IDOR).
threats.mitigation: Verify that the requested object belongs to the caller's tenant before returning it.

threats.description: Missing ownership checks let a tenant perform actions on another tenant's documents.
threats.mitigation: Enforce ownership- and tenant-scoped authorization on every document operation.

threats.description: Tenants share one schema with no row-level security or tenant isolation, so a query flaw or missing filter exposes other tenants' sensitive rows.
threats.mitigation: Enable row-level security keyed on tenant id, or isolate tenants per schema/database.

threats.description: Without tenant isolation, a compromised or buggy query path can modify rows belonging to other tenants.
threats.mitigation: Enforce tenant-scoped access with row-level security and least-privilege database roles.

threats.description: File storage is not partitioned per tenant, so one tenant's prefixes/objects can be read by another despite encryption at rest.
threats.mitigation: Enforce per-tenant prefixes/buckets and scope access policies to the owning tenant.

threats.description: A single global admin role spans all tenants, so a compromised or over-granted admin can affect every tenant.
threats.mitigation: Scope admin roles per tenant and separate platform-admin from tenant-admin duties.

threats.description: The internet-exposed admin portal can be impersonated or targeted by credential attacks to gain tenant-admin access.
threats.mitigation: Enforce MFA and strong session binding for admin authentication.

threats.description: Without per-tenant audit logging, cross-tenant access or changes cannot be attributed to the responsible actor.
threats.mitigation: Enable tenant-scoped audit logging for access to and changes of sensitive rows.

threats.description: File access is not logged per tenant, so unauthorized cross-tenant file reads cannot be traced.
threats.mitigation: Enable per-tenant access logging and retain logs in protected storage.
